title: [jaeger-v2] Map Collector Specific Flags To Corresponding OTEL Configurations
body:
### Requirement

- Part of #5229
- We want to start by mapping the collector specific flags in Jaeger V1 to OTEL using the steps outlined in https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/issues/5229#issuecomment-2372655605 in a google document. 
- If any flags aren't supported by OTEL, we'll discuss how to handle them in this issue.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Most of these flags are for controlling server endpoints (which we should still document). 

The unique ones are these:
  * `--collector.num-workers `
  * `--collector.queue-size`
  * `--collector.queue-size-memory`
  * `--collector.tags`

We should look how they map into various standard components in OTEL, like the batch processor, the attributes processor (which may not be even included in the binary yet).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 couple of questions: 
- For `--collector.queue-size`, can we use map it to the `send_batch_size` in the [batchprocessor](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/processor/batchprocessor/README.md#batch-processor)?
- For `--collector.queue-size-memory`, can we use the [memorylimiterprocessor](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/processor/memorylimiterprocessor/README.md), specifically the `limit_mib` field?
- For `--collector.tags`, can we use the [attributesprocessor](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/processor/attributesprocessor/README.md) where each attribute's key and value match would be passed into `--collector.tags` and action is `insert`?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
- No, 
- maybe,
- probably

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: It's ok to say in the doc if there is no equivalent

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 Sounds good! What's the reason the first one is a no? And do you know of any equivalent to `--collector.queue-size`? I haven't been able to find one so far.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: because Jaeger queue just keeps items in memory until they are processed, and it does not batch spans. It's actually not a great design for resiliency, it's better to have back pressure to the clients.

@participant1 any other action items here? looks like we still don't have a mapping for the following flags
```
--collector.num-workers 
--collector.queue-size
--collector.queue-size-memory
```
Any thoughts on how to proceed?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
* `--collector.num-workers` - I don't see a direct equivalent. gRPC creates new goroutine for each incoming request, there is no "worker pool" that can control concurrency (there is a `MaxConcurrentStreams` setting, but it's only for streaming requests, not unary).  I think we should leave it as unsupported.
* `--collector.queue-size` and `--collector.queue-size-memory` - there is no queue by default. We could consider using [exporterhelper](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/tree/main/exporter/exporterhelper) in the `jaeger_storage_exporter`, which will provide these capabilities.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 we currently have queuing disabled [here](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/main/cmd/jaeger/internal/exporters/storageexporter/factory.go#L44). The exporterhelper queue has a queue size field in the configuration (see https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/exporter/exporterhelper/internal/queue_sender.go#L34). Do we want to expose this in the storage exporter. There isn't anything here to configure memory though.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: yeah, I think we should enable all those features. Do they already have config structs exposed?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 doesn't look like it - see https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/main/cmd/jaeger/internal/exporters/storageexporter/config.go#L17-L19. Should we embed the QueueConfig struct there? Also, are we not going to support the max memory? There's also the [memorylimiterprocessor](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/processor/memorylimiterprocessor/README.md).
